recommendation: VIX-pct (expanding-percentile India VIX, min_obs=252, median/decile splits) stays the state machine that runs sleeve A. Neither HMM variant (f01 2-state, f02 3-state) is promotable to a stress-flag/regime role. The f20 L2-style RV+DD composite is the only candidate that beats VIX-pct on registered bars, but its edge is too thin (effective n~1-2 events) to supersede VIX-pct today; keep it as a monitored candidate, not the sleeve-A trigger.
evidence: f01: HMM2 fwd21d-vol spread is 2.02x VIX-pct's (12.91 vs 6.39 vol pts) but MISSES its own registered bar (<=1.15x = no material gain) -- and the caveat is disqualifying for a live trigger: HMM-high fires on only 6.2% of days (n=177) vs VIX-pct-median's 37.5% (n=1075), and catches only 45% of storm days vs 82% for VIX-pct -- HMM is 'NOT a substitute stress flag' (f01.json caveats, verbatim). f02: adding a 3rd state does not fix onset timing -- 0/41 crash onsets are caught at t-1 by EITHER K2 or K3, and K3 is slower once a crash starts (onset-day reaction 2.4% vs K2's 22.0%, verdict TWO-SIDED landing on the 'nothing' side per the board's CONFIRMED read of f02). K3's only value is post-hoc tail concentration (fwd RV 35.6 vol pts, 62 days, 1.6% occupancy) -- a confirmation label after the fact, not a trigger sleeve A can act on before or during a drawdown. Combined, f01+f02 disqualify any HMM state as the regime input for sleeve A: it under-catches storms in real time and lags at the moment that matters (de-risking before/at onset). f20: the L2-style composite (0.5*RV21pct + 0.5*DDpct, both expanding-percentile, quant/ladder/fast_stress.py) at its primary pct>=0.90 gate PASSES both registered bars on the common n=141-month sample -- left-tail trim +46.63% (bar >=20%) and mean cost +9.68% (bar <=10%) -- and edges VIX-pct-alone by +4.42pp trim / -2.4pp cost, i.e. VIX-pct-alone's own cost at this gate is ~12.1% (12.08=9.68+2.4), which MISSES the <=10% cost bar while L2-style clears it. BUT per the board's PARTIAL verdict on f20 (not overturned here): of the common n=141 bottom-decile months, only 2/14 are flagged by the L2-style overlay (1 by VIX-pct alone), and one of those two -- the 2020-03 COVID month (vrp=-57.44, ~5x the next-worst print) -- is flagged identically by both overlays and dominates the tail mean by construction; the entire +4.42pp L2-vs-VIXpct trim/cost edge reduces to ONE additional flagged month (2019-09, a modest -6.0% print). Effective n behind the 'beats VIX-pct' claim is 1-2 events, not a decile-wide effect, and the grid is unstable at the tails (f20 caveats: at pct>=0.95 VIX-pct's trim collapses to +0.00%, only 6 months, small-sample artifact). Net ranking for sleeve A's regime input: VIX-pct is the only machine with a large-sample (n=1075 high-state days, 82% storm capture per f01) real-time track record and is already the shared convention across the OP-D2 batch (F06, F09, F11, F14, F21 all key off the same expanding VIX percentile); L2-style composite shows a directionally promising but statistically thin (effective n~1-2) improvement that should be tracked, not adopted, until it clears a larger/independent sample; HMM (f01/f02) is excluded outright from any gating role -- its only defensible use is as a post-hoc tail-confirmation label (f02's K3 state), never as sleeve A's entry/de-risk trigger.
confidence: high on excluding HMM (f01 caveat: 45% vs 82% storm capture, MISS on its own 1.15x materiality bar; f02: 0/41 onset capture, slower onset reaction 2.4% vs 22.0%); medium on VIX-pct over L2-style (f20 PASS/PASS is real on printed numbers but the board's PARTIAL finding -- edge concentrated in 1-2 of 141 months -- means the L2-style advantage is not yet robust enough to switch the default).
